- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses 1–3 day trend shifts; adjust for 1–2 day delay in reaction to sentiment changes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.50–0.67 values (neutral/weak), model tends to drift toward mean; apply a “mean-reversion” bias: forecast = prior 10-day average + 10–20% sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- Avoid over-relying on recent high sentiment spikes; if sentiment peaks then drops, model often fails to adjust; use sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.8 per day) to dampen forecast momentum.
